Read the description of the Pawn?
The Pawn is the basic piece of chess.  Eight are stationed in a row on each side.
The Pawn can only move in one direction: Forward, towards the opposite side of the board, one space at a time.
The Pawn does not attack the space in front of it, but instead attacks the pieces to the left and right forward diagonal of itself.
Capturing pieces to its diagonals is the only way in which the Pawn may move sideways.
Finally, should the daring Pawn reach the far end of the board, it may be promoted into any other non-King piece of the player's choice.
Read the description of the Bishop?
Two Bishops are placed on each side of both players' King and Queen.
One is on a white square, the other on a black one.
The Bishop can move and attack any number of spaces, but may only move diagonally.
As such, it is limited to whatever color it starts on for the duration of the game.
Read the description of the Rook?
One Rook starts at each corner of the board, totalling two on each player's side.
The Rook moves and attacks any number of spaces, but may only move in straight lines.
Read the description of the Knight?
Two Knights start on each side, in between the Rooks and Bishops.
The Knight is a unique piece in two ways:
Firstly, its pattern of movement and attack takes the shape of an L. It moves two spaces in one direction, and then one additional space to the side.
Secondly, it possesses the unique ability to 'jump' over pieces.
Unlike other pieces, the Knight is not hindered by opposing pieces, ally or enemy, blocking its path.
Despite their strange movement pattern, they are not restricted in the squares they may reach as the Bishop is.
It is possible for any Knight, starting from any position, to reach any square on the board (given enough turns).
Read the description of the Queen?
Each side has one Queen, which starts to the player's left of their King.
The Queen is regarded as the most valuable attacking piece, as it can move and attack any number of spaces in any direction.
Read the description of the King?
The King is the centerpiece of the game.
Each player has exactly one, stationed to the player's right of the Queen.
The King is a weak piece for two reasons:
The first is that it moves and attacks only one space in any direction.
The second reason is that the King may not move into any position under attack by an opposing piece, otherwise it would place itself in check.
As the object of each game is to checkmate the opposing player's King, this piece should always be protected.
ELIAS: If you have any questions, I will be happy to address them to my fullest ability.
Chess is a two-player game.
One side plays 'White' and the other plays 'Black'.
White always takes the first move.
The objective of the game is to place the enemy's King in checkmate.
This is done as each player takes turns moving one piece at a time across the board.
There are six kinds of pieces in chess: The King, Queen, Knight, Rook, Bishop and Pawn.
Please check the statues in this room for descriptions of each piece's function.
Pieces each move and attack different spaces based on their type.
With the exception of the Knight, pieces cannot move through other pieces, allied or otherwise.
The game operates around the concepts of check and checkmate.
Check refers to a position in which one player's King is under attack by an opposing piece.
This means that, on the opposing player's next turn, the King can be captured.
When a player is in check, their next move MUST remove them from check. No other moves may be taken.
Similarly, a player may not make a move that would place them in check.
Such a move might include moving the King into the path of an opposing piece's attack.
However, it may also include moving away a piece that was blocking an opposing piece from reaching one's King.
In this case, that blocking piece is pinned in place.
In order to get out of check, the King may be moved, a piece may be moved to block the attack on the King, or the attacking piece may be captured.
'Checkmate' is a condition of the game in which no move may be taken by a player in check to remove them from that condition.
In short, it means that there is nothing that player can do to escape having their King captured.
